defect_class: a flag the CLI does not know was silently dropped and the command ran anyway

verify --pagesx 400.effect: scan ran with the DEFAULT page budget (40), not 400

status --dbx nope.db.effect: read the DEFAULT reeflog.db and printed a healthy status for it

status --bogus-flag.effect: status printed, output identical to a correct run

init --db probe2.db (no --program).effect: journal created FIRST, refusal came second (probe2.db left behind)

status --db=other.db.effect: inline form ignored -> read the DEFAULT reeflog.db

verify --pages (no value).effect: ran with the default page budget, no complaint

status --db a --db b.effect: one of the two was picked silently

status --help.effect: ran `status` and printed a health report instead of the usage

typo with intent named.stderr_head: reeflog: error: unknown flag --pagesx (did you mean --pages?)

typo in --db.stderr_head: reeflog: error: unknown flag --dbx (did you mean --db?)

flag without value.stderr_head: reeflog: error: flag --pages needs a value

value is another flag.stderr_head: reeflog: error: flag --db needs a value

duplicate flag.stderr_head: reeflog: error: flag --db given more than once — pass it once

stray positional.stderr_head: reeflog: error: unexpected argument `extra` — this command takes flags only

help prints usage.stdout_head:
reeflog v0 — durable local mailbox for Solana events

USAGE:
  reeflog init  --db <file> --program <pubkey>
  reeflog start --db <file> [--seconds N] [--ws URL] [--rpc URL] [--program <pubkey>]

notes: the refusal happens BEFORE any journal is opened or created
a typo that is close to a real flag names the likely intent; a far-away one does not (a wrong guess is worse than none)
--anchor-slot keeps its documented OPTIONAL value (bare form = anchor at the journal's own window)
status now names the journal it reports on ("db": ...) so a report can be checked against the operator's intent
